title: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue
camera_position: from the southeast, at the NE/SE corner area of Prairie Avenue and 21st Street (inferred from corner lot and visible south side)
creator: unknown photographer
repository: Chicagology (chicagology.com) — website compilation; original holder not credited on page
rights_basis: Website reproduction without credited source or rights statement; original holder and rights unresolved
notes: High-quality albumen-era photograph of the Burnham & Root Sherman house (completed 1876): two-and-a-half storeys of dark brick banded with light stone over a high rusticated stone basement, steep slate roofs with Gothic gabled dormers and iron cresting, a tall corner pavilion with conical/hipped slate roof and finial, carved chimney stacks, a front porch carried on clustered colonnettes reached by a curved stone stair with pierced balustrade, a side bay/oriel on the 21st Street flank, low stone-post-and-iron front fence, parkway trees, plank-guard tree boxes and stone sidewalk. A woman stands on the porch; two children sit at the curb. A numeral '4' is printed lower right (plate/series number). Chicagology gives no source; the CHM holds ICHi-001299 'Sherman house, 2100 Prairie, circa 1890' (marker credit) which may be this or a related view — unverified. Key reference for the 1904 massing; the house stood until 1936 so 1904 appearance should match unless altered after the photo.

notes: Front elevation of the Burnham & Root house at 2009 Prairie (permit Aug 1888, 'three-story dwelling, 27×82' for James S. Price per Inter Ocean 17 Aug 1888, quoted on page; occupied by Max A. Meyer/Mayer, d. 1889): narrow three-storey rough-faced (clinker/tapestry) brick front under a tall ogee/curvilinear gable with finial, rock-faced stone basement, carved stone frieze over a projecting first-floor oriel, Gothic-arched entrance with carved panels, tall chimney stacks. At right, part of 2011 Prairie: rock-faced ashlar Richardsonian front with round-arched entry and corner turret with conical roof. Low stone coping at the lot line, stone sidewalk, granite-sett or macadam street. Appears to be a publication halftone (framed plate). 1904 appearance likely identical. Measurement from quoted permit: 27×82 ft, 3 storeys, $25,000.

title: Residence of W. H. Reid, Chicago.
camera_position: from the west side of Prairie Avenue
date: 1895 (Chicagology file name); Reid NRHP 2003 bibliography cites an illustration in Inland Architect, February 1895
creator: unknown photographer; published plate (probably Inland Architect and News Record, Feb. 1895)
repository: Chicagology (chicagology.com) — website compilation; original holder not credited on page
rights_basis: Website reproduction without credited source or rights statement; original holder and rights unresolved
found_via: Chicagology 2013 Prairie page; Reid NRHP bibliography
notes: Captioned halftone plate 'RESIDENCE OF W. H. REID, CHICAGO.' Shows the new 1894 Beers, Clay & Dutton front: cream brick and terra cotta, entrance portico with Ionic columns and balustraded parapet (parapet now missing), oval windows, central tripartite/Palladian windows, roof balustrade with urn-topped end posts (balustrade now gone). Neighbors visible: at left the rock-faced Richardsonian 2011 Prairie with conical-roofed tower; at right 2017 (gabled, high stoop with iron railing). Iron front fence, stone sidewalk. Essentially the 1904 appearance (house finished 1894). Nomination says the front was cream brick with granite basement; inter Ocean (4 Mar 1894, quoted) gives front 25 ft, depth 90 ft, 14 rooms.

title: Shirley T. High Residence 2021 Prairie Avenue
camera_position: from the northwest, on Prairie Avenue
date: undated (file name suggests 1930; halftone with snow)
creator: unknown
repository: Chicagology (chicagology.com) — website compilation; original holder not credited on page
rights_basis: Website reproduction without credited source or rights statement; original holder and rights unresolved
notes: Coarse-screen halftone captioned 'Shirley T. High Residence'. Shows a three-storey dark brick house with a steep front gable, a round corner tower with conical roof at left, arched entrance up a stone stoop, tall chimney, and a broad north side wing with a second gable; picket fence at right. This form is Queen Anne/Richardsonian of the 1880s — consistent with J. L. High's 1886 purchase and 1887 rear addition (Inter Ocean 20 Aug 1887 permit, quoted) or a rebuild; it is not obviously the late-1870s Adams house. Date unknown (Chicagology file name '1930' is not a holder date; Shirley T. High was James L. High's son) — period left unset. Needs source identification before use for 1904.

notes: Walker Evans' 1946 frontal portrait of 2033: narrow three-storey stone (marble/limestone) Italianate front with a full-height three-sided bay at right, segmental-arched windows with carved hoods, bracketed cornice, pedimented door hood on brackets over double doors, high stone stoop, iron fence. notes: Front elevation of the Kelley/Armour house: three storeys of pale (stuccoed or painted) stone-trimmed masonry in Second Empire style, quoined and banded, round-arched windows with keystones, central arched entrance under a carved pediment with a high stone stair with stepped stone cheek walls, patterned slate mansard with arched pedimented dormers and iron cresting, tall chimney. title: 2140 Prairie Ave. (first photograph on Chicagology page, file name "2140prairie1880")
camera_position: from the southeast corner of Prairie Avenue and 22nd Street, looking northwest across the intersection
date: undated; file name says 1880 but the Romanesque house with round tower at right (consistent with Cobb's 1890 Murdoch house at 2130) indicates after 1890
creator: unknown
repository: Chicagology (chicagology.com) — website compilation; original holder not credited on page
rights_basis: Website reproduction without credited source or rights statement; original holder and rights unresolved
notes: Large clear photograph of the Van Osdel–designed Tucker/Byron L. Smith house on the NW corner of 22nd: dark brick with stone bands, three tall conical-roofed round/polygonal corner towers with cresting and finials, Gothic gabled dormers, clustered chimneys; tall iron picket fence on brick piers with ball finials; an iron-and-glass arched porte-cochère/entrance canopy on the 22nd Street (south) side. At right (north) a rough-faced stone house with a conical-roofed rounded bay — very probably 2130 Murdoch (H. I. Cobb, 1890) — and beyond it a long three-storey brick row. Overhead trolley wires and rails in 22nd Street, a cast-iron street lamp at right, a man with a bicycle. Strong 1904 evidence: shows the corner, the fence, the canopy and the trolley wires; date window inferred c. 1890–1911.
